meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm sorry, I have twenty minutes before a client call. Why did my son find out about a zero from the gradebook on his phone, in the middle of class?
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Go on, Hale. What do you have that says the zero should have been entered at all?

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.

I'm writing down 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58. A late night isn't proof of anything, Hale, and a teenager typing fast at the last minute is not a crime. Show me the history itself, and tell me who else has seen it.
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.

I'm searching it myself, Hale, and I'm writing down the line exactly as you said it. A misquoted line is a bad quotation, not a finding about who wrote the essay. Did anyone put that line to Owen before the zero went in?

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.

Section 4.4, I have it printed, Hale. Before I say anything about Thursday, I want in writing that nothing goes on his record and that no student sees or hears about it. You also still haven't told me whether anyone put that line to Owen before the zero went in.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. The zero must come off, I need written confirmation that nothing goes on Owen's record and that no student sees or hears of this, and I need to know whether anyone put that line to Owen before the zero was entered. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: the fallback position, with nothing agreed; she still wants the zero withdrawn, a written promise that nothing goes on his record and that it stays private, and an answer on whether Owen was asked about the quoted line.
What moved her: "that was wrong", because owning the early zero in one sentence earned a flat okay, and the dated times that followed kept her listening and moved her off her opening position.
What cost ground: nothing.
Try next time: answer her question about whether Owen was spoken to before the zero, and do it before you offer Thursday's rewrite, since she asked twice and the offer landed without it.
